chokhmat-shlomo/1:_.he: סעיף א' הקובר את מתו בתוך הרגל לא חל עליו אבילות ברגל וכו'. נ"ב בא מעשה ידי באחד שנעשה אבל בחג הסוכות ר"ל והוריתי לו להתיר לעלות לתורה בשמחת תורה והיינו בזה כיון דנוהגין כל העולם לעלות לתורה אם לא יעלה האבל לתורה הוי פרהסיא ואף דיש לחלק דהתם היה נוהג ר"ת לעלות במקום הזה והוי פרהסיא אבל כאן אולי עלה במקום אחר וכיוצא בזה כתב הרש"ל בתשובה סי' ע"א לענין אבל המל בנו שאינו עולה לתורה מכל מקום י"ל הכא טעם אחריתא הוי כיון דמבואר בש"ע דבער"ה מותר לאבל לצאת מביתו לו' סליחות אף דבשאר ימים אסור לאבל לצאת מ"מ בזה כיון דהעולם מרבים בסליחות הוי לו צער אם ישב הוא בביתו א"כ ה"נ כיון דבשמחת תורה נהגו כל ישראל לעלות לתורה איכא צערא אם ישב הוא ולא יעלה לתורה והוי דמי כמו התם דמותר לצאת מביתו ועוד נראה דזה דומה למ"ש הט"ז הלכות שבת סי' רמ"ד לענין מלאכת מחובר דאינו מותר מכח מראית עין רק באם יש ב' צדדים להתיר אבל אם יש רק צד אחד להתיר חיישינן דלמא ידע זה דאינו בקיבולת וכו' ויסבור שהוא שכיר יום ע"ש כן ה"נ בזה. בשלמא במי שמל בנו יש שני צדדים להיתר אחד דלמא לא ידעו כלל שהיום יום מילת בנו ואם אין לו מילת בנו אין לו היום בלא"ה לעלות לתורה ואף אם ידעו שהיום מל בנו אכתי אולי עלה כבר בבהכ"נ אחר ולכך איכא תרי צדדי להתירא ולכך לא חיישינן לפרהסיא. אבל בשמחת תורה כיון שהכל עולין לתורה היום ואין צד היתר רק מכח אולי עליו במקום אחר שפיר יש לחוש אולי ידעו רבים שלא עלה במקום אחר ויכירו כי מכח האבילות היא נמנע מלעלות והוי פרהסיא. הן אמת דיש לחלק בין נדון הט"ז לנדון דידן די"ל עכ"פ פרהסיא לא הוי מכל מקום כיון דמלתא דרבנן בעלמא היא בפרט ברגל דלא חלה עליו אבילות וגם מכח טעם הנ"ל שצער הוא לו דיש להקל כה"ג וזה ברור ונכון לדינא ודוק היטב:
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_.en: Seif 1: One who buries his dead during the festival — mourning does not apply during the festival, etc. — note: a case came before me where someone became a mourner on Sukkot, Hashem spare us, and I instructed him to permit ascending to the Torah on Simchat Torah; and this was because since everyone is accustomed to ascend to the Torah, if the mourner does not ascend to the Torah it is public display [of mourning]; and even though one may distinguish that there he was accustomed to ascend to the Torah in that place and it was public display, but here perhaps he ascended elsewhere — and similarly wrote Maharshal in responsum siman 71 regarding a mourner who circumcised his son, that he does not ascend to the Torah — nevertheless one may say here there is another reason, namely since it is clear in Shulchan Aruch that on erev Rosh Hashana a mourner is permitted to leave his house to recite selichot even though on other days a mourner may not leave — nevertheless here, since the public increases in selichot, it is distress for him if he sits in his house; if so, here too since on Simchat Torah all Israel are accustomed to ascend to the Torah, there is distress if he sits and does not ascend to the Torah, and it is comparable to there that he is permitted to leave his house. And further it appears this is similar to what Taz wrote in laws of Shabbat siman 244 regarding attached melacha, that it is not permitted based on marit ayin except when there are two sides to permit; but if there is only one side to permit we are concerned perhaps this one knows he is not in a binding agreement, etc., and will think he is a day laborer, see there — so too here. Granted, for one who circumcised his son there are two sides for permission: one, perhaps they did not know at all that today is the day of his son's circumcision; and if he has no circumcision today, in any case he has no obligation today to ascend to the Torah; and even if they knew he circumcised his son today, still perhaps he already ascended in another synagogue — therefore there are two sides to permit and therefore we are not concerned for public display. But on Simchat Torah, since everyone ascends to the Torah that day and there is no side of permission except based on 'perhaps he ascended elsewhere,' properly one should be concerned perhaps many knew he did not ascend elsewhere and will recognize that because of mourning he refrains from ascending — and it is public display. It is true one may distinguish between Taz's case and our case, that one may say in any case there is no public display, since it is merely a d'rabbanan matter, especially during the festival when mourning did not apply to him; and also based on the above reason that it is distress for him, there is room to be lenient in such a case — and this is clear and correct for practical law — examine well.

chokhmat-shlomo/2:_.he: (שם סעיף ה') אעפ"י שאין אבילות נוהג במועד אנינות נוהג כו וכו'. נ"ב הנה נשאלתי במת ביו"ט ב' ולא היו מניחין אותו לקברו עד סמוך לערב עפ"י דת המלך יר"ה אם שייך בזה דין אנינות אם לאו. והשבתי דנראה פשוט דנוהג בזה אנינות דאף שכתב המג"א דהיכי דא"א לקברו מחמת איד עכו"ם דלא חל אנינות היינו אם כל היום אי אפשר לקברו אבל אם היום אפשר לקברו רק אחר זמן מה גוף היום לא מחלקינן וכל שהיום יהיה נקבר שייך ביה אנינות. ואינו דומה למה דקיי"ל דבמת ביו"ט דאז בלילה יקדש ולא חל עליו אנינות היינו נמי דלילה ויום השינוי ניכר והם גופין מחולקין לכך לא חל עליו אנינות בינתים אבל ביום גופא שאין השינוי ניכר לא פסקינן ליה לשנים. והנה יש שהיו רוצים להביא ראיה ממ"ש המג"א לעיל סי' תקכ"ו דאפשר דס"ל כיון דאין דעתו לקברו עד אחר האכילה לא חל עליהם דין אנינות עד אחר אכילה ע"ש וא"כ ה"ה נמי בזה. אבל לדעתי הנה גוף דברי המג"א המה תמוהין דאם יש סברא לחלק כן מה ראיה מביא הרא"ש בפ"ג דברכות מן הרמב"ם שאין אנינות ביו"ט ממה שהיה מצוה להביא לפניו שופר להוציאו י"ח ומה ראייה היא דלמא התם הוי דעתו לקברן אחר האכילה לכך לא חל עליו דין אנינות אבל היכי דדעתו לקברן מקודם יש דין אנינות ביו"ט ובע"כ דליתא להך סברא. מיהו גם לדברי המג"א אינו דומה חדא הרי חזינן דהמג"א דייק דוקא אם דעתו לקברו אחר האכילה הא אם הוי דעתו לקברו אחר התפלה היו פטורין מן התפלה ובע"כ דבעינן דבר אחר המפסיק בינתיים בין המצוה בין הקבורה יהיה דבר אחר המפסיק וניכר החילוק בזה דומה ליום ולילה שבלילה לא חל עליו דין אנינות כן ה"נ בזה אבל אם אין שינוי המפסיק בנתים פטור מן התפלה וא"כ ה"נ כיון דבין שעה שאין מניחין אותו לקברו בין שעה שיניחוהו לקברו ליכא שינוי הניכר. דבשלמא התם כיון דבאכילה תליא מלתא והוי דבר התלוי במעשה והוי ניכר לכך שייך לחלק ביום מתקנינן ולכך פריך כיון דהוי החשש מכח שבות דאין מקדשין טפי נא' שלא ישא עתה דאם ישאנה עתה אולי תמות אשתו והוי אונן טפי עדיף להמתין לישא אותה ביוה"כ ואז כיון שיראה דבעי למימת קדם וכנסה להך כעין דפריך הש"ס שם כעין זה ע"ש כן י"ל בזה כיון דחזי דבעי למימת קדם וכנסה ועל תנאי אם תמות האחרת ולא הוי ב' בתים ואז אם תמות חל עליו ימי משתה למפרע ולא יהיה נעשה אונן עוד וא"כ טפי ראוי שלא לחוש לאיסור שבות משא"כ עתה דכנסה קודם והרי בעינן חופה הראויה לביאה ובשלמא ביוה"כ יהיה החופה הראויה לביאה בערב וזה נחשב ראויה לביאה כמ"ש בחידושינו מכבר ע"ש אבל אם נושא מקודם הרי כל שבעת ימים מפרישין אותו מביתו ובע"כ דנושאה מקודם א"כ כבר כלו שבעת ימי המשתה קודם יוה"כ לכך יהיה לו דין אונן כן אזיל קושית הש"ס דטפי הו"ל לחוש לאיסור אנינות מן איסור שבות דאין מקדשין ודוק כי קצרתי. ומוכח מזה דאף בלא בעל חל עליו ימי משתה תחלה ואין לו אף דין אונן דהרי ביוה"כ לא יהיה בועל ופריך כן והבן כי קצרתי. והנה שבתי וראיתי שזה טעות מכמה טעמי דאף ששבעת ימי המשתה דוחין אבלות מ"מ אין דוחין אנינות אם רוצים לקברו היום דלא עדיפי מיו"ט דנוהג בו אנינות אם קברו היום ולו' דהרי דעתו לקברו היום זה קשה בלא זה כנ"ל. ועוד הרי קידושין בלא חופה לאו ביתו הוא ובע"כ דכניס לה וא"כ שוב אי אפשר לו' על תנאי דאין תנאי בחופה ועוד ממ"נ אם יקדשנה מעכשיו הדר אם תמות ראשונה הו"ל עבודה בשתי בתים למפרע ואם יקדשנה רק בתנאי אם תמות א"כ אם תמות חייל עליו אנינות מתחלה ואח"כ השמחה ועוד הרי הש"ס מסיק דאין קושייתו מכח אנינות רק דלמא מטריד והרי זה לא יתוקן אף אם יקדשנה ויכנסנה ויחול עליו ימי משתה מכל מקום אטרודי מי לא מטריד והרי סוף סוף אי אפשר לתקן הדבר ולכך ליתנייהו להני מילי שכתבנו ומכל מקום משנה לא זזה ממקומה לפלפול בעלמא ודוק היטב:
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_.en: (There seif 5) Although mourning does not apply during the festival, onen status applies, etc., etc. — note: I was asked about a deceased on the second day of Yom Tov whom they would not permit to bury until near evening per the king's law, Hashem spare us — whether onen status applies here or not. I answered it seems obvious onen status applies here, for even though Magen Avraham wrote where it is impossible to bury because of non-Jewish dominion onen status does not apply — that is if impossible all day; but if possible to bury him today only after a time, what difference does the day make — we do not split it, and whoever will be buried today, onen status applies to him. And it is not comparable to what is established regarding a deceased on Yom Tov — that then at night he becomes impure and onen status does not apply to him — namely, also night and day the change is evident and they are separate entities, therefore onen status did not apply to him in the interim; but on the day itself, where the change is not evident, we do not split it into two. And behold some wished to bring proof from what Magen Avraham wrote above siman 526 that perhaps he holds since his intent is not to bury until after the meal, onen status did not apply to them until after the meal, see there — if so, here too. But in my opinion behold Magen Avraham's words themselves are astonishing — if there is reason to distinguish thus, what proof does the Rosh bring in chapter 3 of Berachot from the Rambam that there is no onen status on Yom Tov from that they had to bring a shofar before him to take him out on the 18th — what proof is it? Perhaps there his intent was to bury them after the meal, therefore onen status did not apply to him; but where his intent is to bury them earlier, there is onen status on Yom Tov — and perforce this view does not exist. However, even according to Magen Avraham's words it is not comparable: one, behold we see Magen Avraham was precise only if his intent is to bury after the meal — but if his intent is to bury after prayer they would be exempt from prayer, and perforce we require something else interrupting in the interim between the mitzvah and the burial — something else interrupting and the distinction evident in this, similar to day and night where at night onen status did not apply to him — so too here; but if there is no interrupting change in the interim, exempt from prayer — if so, here too, since between the hour they do not permit him to be buried and the hour they will permit him to be buried there is no evident change. For granted there, since the matter depends on the meal and it is a matter dependent on action and evident — therefore one may split the day itself; but between hours where the change is not evident, it is impossible to split the day itself into two. And further, granted after the meal, since this is a fixed time for all deceased and it is known that today they do not bury except after the meal — therefore there is no disgrace to the deceased, for all know it is not his burial time until after the meal; but here, per the king's law, since hours are not all equal and there is a deceased they leave to bury in the morning when his time has ended — who will know this one is not buried because his time has not ended? Therefore it is disgrace to the deceased if they engage in prayer; and behold for this reason an onen is forbidden to be stringent based on honor of the deceased — so too here disgrace of the deceased applies, therefore forbidden to pray. And it is as if they do not permit him all day to be buried — onen status does not apply there, for when the public sees they did not bury him all day, all will know it is because burial was impossible and there is no disgrace to the deceased since burial is literally another day; but on that day itself, if burial will be that day, one may say from laxity they delay him — then one may split the day itself into two where there is no fixed time for all deceased equally; therefore they certainly have onen status. And likewise if there is delay — they do not wish to permit burial until tomorrow but the onenim have ability to strive to bury him today near evening — onen status also applies in the morning. And it is not comparable to one in captivity who did not despair of burial — onen status does not apply to him, only mourning — for there he is not yet buried at all; therefore even though they can strive to bury him, since it is in doubt he has no onen status; but here it is known he will be buried tomorrow, and since he will certainly be buried tomorrow and it is also possible through striving he will be buried today, onen status applies from today. And especially there it deals with something depending on much money and it is doubtful whether it will help — therefore onen status did not apply to them; but here with a small sum it helps and it is close to certain it will help — therefore onen status applies to them; and on the contrary it appears that because of this onen status applies from now even if they will not bury him until after the meal or after the festival ends — nevertheless from now this striving applies to them, and therefore it is like one who darkens before the boundary — onen status applies from when he begins to darken before the boundary — so too here. And this is correct for practical law that they are exempt from all mitzvot like other onenim on Yom Tov; and see clear proof to this from Magen Avraham's own words siman 496 s.k. 6 — it is proven there that even though by law burial is forbidden until after the megillah, nevertheless onen status applies and he is exempt — all the more so here, see there and examine; and even for Magen Avraham's conclusion there, it was only regarding megillah, for megillah precedes burial of the deceased as Magen Avraham wrote; and also in the book Avnei Nezer disagrees with Magen Avraham — also there; but in our case certainly he is not permitted to pray — examine well. (There) And if he died on Yom Tov and does not wish to bury him that day, onen status does not apply to him, etc. — note: from this it is clear that even if his intent is to bury at night, nevertheless there is no onen status on Yom Tov since he has no intent to bury that day — all the more so on Shabbat and Yom Kippur when burial is forbidden that day, there is no onen status. And I was very astonished from the Gemara Yoma daf 13 that asks: and R' Yehuda — even another wife they prepare for him lest his wife die — and if his wife dies in the middle of the service is he an onen, etc. — what does it ask? And what compares Yom Kippur to weekday? Behold one may say on Yom Kippur, since if possible to bury her today onen status does not apply to him — and one should not say that for onen in kodshim we do not follow whether he can bury or not — from where to challenge thus? And perhaps also for onen status in kodshim onen status applies only if he wishes to bury that day — for this is learned from the verse of Aharon 'on that very day they offered,' etc., and there burial was given that day; but without burial being given, perhaps onen status does not apply at all — why does it ask? And requires further study. And even though there is one tanna in Moed Katan that Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur are not like festivals — nevertheless what does it ask? And let us say R' Yehuda holds like the one who says Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur are like festivals and therefore onen status does not apply if he does not bury that day — end of the matter that it requires further study — examine. And see in my work on Orach Chayim from the year 5596 section 132 that a certain scholar named our teacher R' Eikel from the community of Botoshatsh wished to refute the above difficulty and I refuted all his words and the difficulty stands in its place — see there well. And behold when I was speaking in the sugya of Yoma there, it seems to decide from this what Taz and Shach dispute in Yoreh De'ah siman 391, and Nekudas HaKesef brought the dispute of early authorities whether mourning befell a groom after chuppah who has not yet consummated — whether mourning applies first or the seven days of festivity, see there. In my humble opinion one may prove from this: at first glance it is difficult — why does the Gemara ask that R' Yehuda said lest his wife die and if she dies he performs service — behold he is an onen, etc. — why does it ask? And perhaps where possible to fix they fix, and what is impossible they do not fix; and especially since the Gemara concludes in Sukkah that R' Yehuda was not concerned for death except based on a general virtue he was concerned for death — if so, it works for what relates to atonement for all Israel; but for what relates to prohibition of onen status and lest he eat in this we are not concerned for death — why does it ask? And one must say the Gemara understood from R' Yehuda's language that he said 'they prepare another wife for him' — perforce he married before Yom Kippur, for if on Yom Kippur there would be no need for preliminary invitation, not like the Yerushalmi — therefore it is difficult to him why he does not marry on Yom Kippur; and perforce based on rabbinic enactment one does not betroth on Shabbat and Yom Tov, and where possible to fix so he does not come to this they fix — therefore it asks: since the concern is from rabbinic enactment not to betroth, better he should not marry now — for if he marries her now perhaps his wife will die and he will be an onen; better to wait to marry her on Yom Kippur, and then since he will see he needs to die first and marry her for that — like the kind the Gemara asks there — so one may say here: since he sees he needs to die first and marry, and conditionally if the other dies and he will not have two homes — then if she dies mourning days of festivity apply retroactively and he will not become an onen again; if so, better not to be concerned for rabbinic prohibition of betrothal than now that he married beforehand and behold we require a chuppah fit for consummation. And granted on Yom Kippur the chuppah fit for consummation will be in the evening and this is considered fit for consummation as I wrote in my novellae already, see there; but if he marries beforehand, behold all seven days they separate him from his house — perforce he marries beforehand — if so, the seven days of festivity already ended before Yom Kippur, therefore he will have onen status — so goes the Gemara's difficulty, that better to be concerned for prohibition of onen status than rabbinic prohibition of betrothal — examine, for I abbreviated. And it is proven from this that even without consummation mourning days of festivity apply first and he has no onen status — for behold on Yom Kippur he will not consummate, and it asks thus — understand, for I abbreviated. And behold I reconsidered and saw this is an error for several reasons: for even though seven days of festivity override mourning, nevertheless they do not override onen status if they wish to bury that day — it is no better than Yom Tov where onen status applies if they bury that day; and one should not say behold his intent is to bury that day — this is difficult without this, as above. And further, behold betrothal without chuppah is not his home — perforce he brought her in — if so, again impossible to say conditionally, for there is no condition in chuppah; and further from either way: if he betroths her now, again if the first dies he would have service in two homes retroactively; and if he betroths her only conditionally if she dies — then if she dies onen status applies from the start and afterward festivity; and further behold the Gemara concludes his difficulty is not from onen status, only lest he be troubled — and behold this will not be fixed even if he betroths and brings her in and mourning days of festivity apply — nevertheless will he not be troubled?
